items.title: 68146_Russell Procope oral history interview
items.q: In the meantime I got a letter from my brother who was overseas, in General Patton's Army

ctx.x: But as it turned out I went back to my regiment and the Colonel -- the Colonel had what everyone called untouchables. I was one of the Colonel's untouchables. When you came to get soldiers, he had a file on this side that was the untouchables, and there was a file on that side which was the touchables. I was one of the untouchables. So the Colonel transferred me to the medics. I became a member of the Medical Corps, which I loved. It was beautiful. I loved that sort of thing, you know. I found I loved it, you…
In the meantime I got a letter from my brother who was overseas, in General Patton's Army, and he said to me, "Whatever you can do to keep from coming overseas, you do it."

"Even if it means going to jail." He said, "You go to jail. Don't come over here." Because my brother went all the way across the channel, clean on to Berlin with General Patton, and he saw the worst of it. He came back from the war with six battle stars. Yes, sir.
